study_identification.author_journal_year: Han S et al., Psychological Medicine, 2024
study_identification.title: Shared differential factors underlying individual spontaneous neural activity abnormalities in major depressive disorder

study_characteristics.study_objective: To parse individualized Amplitude of Low-Frequency Fluctuations (ALFF) abnormalities in Major Depressive Disorder (MDD) by hypothesizing that they can be represented as a linear combination of shared differential factors. The study also aims to explore the neurobiological relevance of these factors and their potential for identifying depressive subtypes.

hc_age.answer: Discovery dataset: mean 33.96, sd 19.25; Validation dataset: mean 36.15, sd 24.552

hc_sex.answer: Discovery dataset: F 613 (56.81%), M 466 (43.19%); Validation dataset: F 641 (58.06%), M 463 (41.94%)

quality_checking_detail.answer: Rigorous quality control for both clinical and imaging data. Friston-24 head-motion parameters, white matter and cerebrospinal fluid signals were regressed out. A scrubbing procedure was performed.

site_effect_handling_detail.answer: Combat harmonization was independently performed in each dataset to minimize site effect on ALFF values.

modeling_method.answer: Gaussian process regression; Non-negative matrix factorization (NMF)

software_tool.answer: DPARSF (version 5.4); GAUSSIAN PROCESS REGRESSION AND CLASSIFICATION Toolbox version 4.2; scikit-learn (version 1.3.0)

nm_vldtn_handle_ns.reason: The study used ComBat harmonization to handle site effects, which is a method for addressing nuisance structure.
nm_vldtn_handle_ns.supporting_text: Combat harmonization was independently performed in each dataset to minimize site effect on ALFF values (Johnson, Li, & Rabinovic, 2007) in each dataset independently.

nm_vldtn_same_domain_nonindep.reason: The study performed 10-fold cross-validation to evaluate the model performance.
nm_vldtn_same_domain_nonindep.supporting_text: Model performance was assessed by calculating the standardized mean squared error (MSE) between the true ALFF values and predicted ones (Marquand et al., 2016).

nm_vldtn_same_domain_indep.supporting_text: leave-one-site-out cross-validation, where one set served as the testing site and the remaining as the training set;

nm_vldtn_diff_domain.reason: The study trained the model on the discovery dataset and tested it on the validation dataset, and vice versa.
nm_vldtn_diff_domain.supporting_text: training a Gaussian process regression model based on HCs in the discovery dataset and applying it to HCs in the validation dataset, and vice versa;

clinical_application_and_analysis.association_analysis: Multilinear model; Pearson correlation; two-sample t-test; Gaussian mixture model (GMM)
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_brief: The study identified four robust and reproducible shared factors that underlie individual-specific spontaneous neural activity abnormalities in MDD, which were associated with clinical characteristics and neurobiological features, and facilitated the identification of four distinct depressive subtypes.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_detailed: The study identified two positive and two negative factors underlying ALFF abnormalities in MDD. These factors were associated with clinical features like medication status and symptom severity. They also correlated with neurotransmitter receptor/transporter distributions, inflammation-related gene expression, and connectome-informed epicenters. The factor compositions were used to identify four reproducible subtypes of MDD with distinct ALFF patterns and clinical characteristics.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_limitations: The study had insufficient clinical information, such as symptom dimensions and comorbidities. A quantitative analysis of the relationship between changes in factor compositions and medication variables was not conducted. The study only included cross-sectional data, which restricts insights into the evolution of differential factors with disease progression.
clinical_application_and_analysis.application_notes: The identified differential factors and subtypes could potentially be used for personalized diagnosis and treatment of MDD.
